note: One data structure for the four families of axKit and the links between them, asked by the maintainer on 2026-11-16 so that he and the assistant name the same things by the same short names. It describes what the code does today, read from the code that day; it changes no behaviour. Since 2026-11-17 the kinds of event and the sounds are in code too (AxKit.Core/Events: EventKind, EventSound and the table EventPresenter), held to this file both ways by EventKindTests, and every sound is played by raising its kind at the door (AxKit.Forms/EventDoor; docs/axKit/events.md, section 10). Each of the four lists has the same shape, a family with its members. The keys stay in docs/axKit/key-families.json and the commands in docs/axKit/window-commands.json; this file names them and does not copy them. Where the same kind of event sounds one way in one place and another way elsewhere, the event's note says so: those are the open choices, and a sound is added or changed only when the maintainer has chosen it by ear (docs/axKit/earcons.md).
chain: Read it as a chain. Something starts (your own hands, the program underneath, an AI, axKit itself, Windows). When it is your hands, a key or a menu runs a function, a command of the window. The function ends in an event, a kind of thing that happened. The event has a sound or none, and words or none. Events that nobody's hands started enter the chain at the event.

actions.title: Your own hands
actions.learn: What you do yourself, in the window that has the focus or from anywhere in Windows. Only these run a command without anything being asked or said about who ran it.

members.title: A key of the window
members.what: A key of one of the families of keys (docs/axKit/key-groups.md). It runs the command that holds it, or it is the control's own key, as the arrows are.

members.title: Typing
members.what: Characters typed into a field. Typing is no command: NVDA echoes it and axKit says nothing, except in a text's navigation mode, where a letter is a command or is refused.

members.title: A menu item
members.what: A command chosen from the menu bar or the Context menu.

members.title: The command palette
members.what: Ctrl+Shift+P, words typed, a line chosen with Enter. It runs what the menu item runs, and says a check item's new state since no menu shows it.

members.title: A key from anywhere in Windows
members.what: Ctrl+Shift with Space or a punctuation key, in any program: it brings up axStart, axClip or axHelp.

actions.title: The program under an access layer
actions.learn: A program axKit runs and reads for you: Claude Code, a shell, Git, KeePassXC's tool, an MCP server, the media engine, an installer. What it prints, asks and ends with reaches you as events you did not start at that moment.

members.title: The program underneath
members.what: Its output, its questions, its state (working, ready), its end.

actions.title: An AI
actions.learn: An AI client the user paired, or AI help. What an AI starts always says so (rule 11): the words name who ran or asks, and anything that acts outside the window asks first.

members.title: An AI tool's call
members.what: A paired AI client runs a command of a window by name, offers a command for you to run, adds a task, opens an app, or asks to be paired.

members.title: AI help answering
members.what: Claude's answer to Shift+F1 or Ask about this window, which comes up to a minute after you asked.

actions.title: axKit itself
actions.learn: What axKit does on its own: something it started for you ends later, a wait runs out, or another axKit window hands something over.

members.title: Work of axKit's that ends later
members.what: A copy, a git command, a download, an install, a report being sent, a workflow run, a search of every list: started by your command, finished in the background.

members.title: A wait that ran out
members.what: A timer: axPass locking after idle minutes, the repeating chord of background work, a question shown once Claude is idle.

members.title: Another axKit window
members.what: A second start that hands its file or text to the window already open, or a hotkey app bringing a window up.

actions.title: Windows
actions.learn: The system around axKit. axKit looks at these when its window comes to the front, not all the time.

members.title: Windows
members.what: The clipboard changed, a file or folder changed on disk, the window came to the front or went behind, the computer was locked, the colours changed.

actions.title: The automated checks
actions.learn: Only in a test run, on a desktop of its own, never in your windows.

members.title: A window script
members.what: The runner presses the key a command has now, or chooses its menu item (docs/axKit/command-language.md CL-2.1).

marks.learn: It says or shows something and changes nothing.
It opens a window or a file, or moves within the window.
It changes the window's own state or the file the window holds.
It reaches outside the window: it deletes, moves, sends, starts a program, writes the clipboard or uses the network. An AI tool must ask before one runs.

functions.learn: What the window holds as a whole: open, new, save, refresh, restart, hide, exit, and the same place opened in another app.
Go somewhere in what the window holds: find, the next heading, link or list, go to a line, a bookmark, the next file.
Do something with the whole of what the window holds: undo and redo, run, push and pull, a new item, interrupt.
Do something with the one thing the focus is on: copy, cut, paste, rename, delete, open, information. Shift+F10 and Ctrl+Period open it.
Settings, each said with its new state: text, speech, sounds, announcements, what happens when something is done.
The other windows of axKit: a new window of any app, close all windows, say the status.
The services of the whole bundle: the AI tools and what they may do, Claude for AI help, the theme.
The keys (F1), the user guide, the command palette, sending a report (F4), about, diagnostics and the key test.
Commands that are a key with no menu item, because their meaning depends on where the focus is: Tab between panes, Enter on a row, Right into a list, F3 for find next. An AI tool never runs these.
Not commands at all: the keys a control handles itself, the arrows in a list or a text and typing in a field. The inventory does not hold them; the families of keys do.

events.title: What came of your own command
events.learn: You pressed a key, typed, or chose a command, and this is how it ended. Every command ends in one of these kinds, so nothing you do is ever silent. An AI tool that runs a command gets the same ending, with the words that say who ran it in front.

members.when: You typed a character into a field.
members.words: None from axKit: NVDA echoes what you type.

members.when: The key or command moved you, and there is something there.
members.words: NVDA reads the new place itself, or axKit says it: 'docs, 5 items, plan.md', 'Line 12 of 80', 'Install, heading level 2'.

members.when: The move landed on a heading of a text or on a section row of a list.
members.words: The heading itself, read after the sound.
members.apps: Texts with Markdown headings (axDown, axPreview), the text of every notice, and the section rows of the item windows (axTask, axPass, axMCP, axAutomate).
members.note: Not in the conversations of axClaude and axTerminal, and not in axJSON.

members.when: In a text's navigation mode, a letter was taken as a command that has somewhere to go.
members.words: What the jump lands on, after the sound.
members.apps: Every text of several lines that you can type in, while it is in navigation mode.
members.note: Only for a letter alone. The same jump with Ctrl, from the menu or from the palette has no sound before it.

members.when: The command ran and there is nothing of that kind to go to: no next heading, no match, nothing found.
members.words: Often the reason: 'No next heading', 'No commands match x', 'Nothing found for x', 'Not found'. Sometimes none.
members.note: Not one sound today. Nothing (the low buzz) only for a letter in navigation mode. Edge for a typed name that no entry starts with, for the palette and the hotkey windows with no match, for a section or heading jump in the item windows, and for axTask's search of every list. No sound at all, only words, for a Ctrl jump in an editor, for Find ('Not found') and for axFile's filter.

members.when: Nothing further that way: the first or last entry of a list, the top level, a row that cannot be gone into, the end of the history, a key that selects as it moves at an end of the list.
members.words: None in a plain list. In the palette, the hotkey windows and axFile's folder field, the entry you are on is said again. 'Top of the fields', 'A section: Down goes into it'.
members.note: Two places give words and no sound for the same thing: axMedia's 'First file' and 'End of queue' on Ctrl+Shift+Left and Right, and axFile's 'Top' on Backspace at This PC, where Left at the same place plays the edge.

members.when: The key has no command where you are.
members.words: None, or the reason: 'No action on Ctrl+4 in this list'.
members.apps: Navigation mode of a text; the item windows; every window for Ctrl+Enter.
members.note: Unassigned (the wooden bonk) only for a plain key that would type in navigation mode. Edge for Ctrl+Enter where the window has no main action, for Ctrl+Space where there is no text with modes, for Space on a row that cannot be checked, and for an action key with no action. A key no window knows gets nothing from axKit.

members.when: The change you asked for is not allowed here and nothing changed: navigation mode, a read-only text, a locked database, a form with a field still empty.
members.words: None for a key in navigation mode. From a menu, the palette or an AI tool the reason: 'Navigation mode: press Ctrl+Space to edit'. 'Not a task', 'Select an item first', 'Type the field's title'.
members.note: Some refusals have words and no sound: 'Read only: there is no edit mode here', axPass's 'Locked: Enter unlocks', axAutomate's 'This version views and runs the workflows'.

members.when: A command that only tells you something said it: the status, the line number, the current folder.
members.words: The information itself.

members.when: A setting or a state of the window changed.
members.words: The new state: 'Word wrap off', 'Text size 14', 'Navigation mode', 'checked'. From the palette, 'Word wrap, checked'.
members.note: A plain menu toggle says nothing by itself where its own code does not; run by an AI tool, only 'Claude ran Word wrap' is sure to be said.

members.when: The command did its work at once.
members.words: A few words: 'Saved', 'Copied', 'Undone: rename', 'Refreshed: Processes', 'Pasted, 3 lines'.

members.when: Your message, command or answer went out to the program underneath.
members.words: 'Sent', 'Queued', 'Sent, not recorded', 'Sent: 1, Green'. In axClaude the word is a setting; in axTerminal it is always said.
members.note: In axClaude the sound plays a second time, with no words, when axClaude itself confirms the review after your last answer.

members.when: An earlier command came back into the field from the history.
members.words: The command, or 'blank'.

members.when: The command asks before it acts: 'Delete a.txt?', 'Save changes to notes.md?', a consent before the first connection.
members.words: The question, read as the notice opens; the answers are a list or buttons.

members.when: Something opened at your command: a help text, the palette, a field or a form in the window, another axKit window, an outside program.
members.words: NVDA reads what opened. 'Started Notepad', 'Opening x' for an outside program.
members.note: The focus arriving in a list, a text, a field or a form has a kind of its own since 2026-11-22, raised by the component itself: form-entered, list-entered, field-entered, text-entered. This kind is what is left: another window, an outside program.

members.when: The focus entered a form from outside it: several things asked for one action, Tab between them (SPEC AX-7.11). Once for the form; moving between its controls is silent.
members.words: After NVDA has read the first control: the title and the one word, 'Move 2 items, form'. The explanation is not said: Ctrl+Q reads it. Two forms say their text after the word, since it is what will happen and not how a form is used: the report, and an action of an axTask list.
members.apps: Every window with a form: the report (F4), axTask's item form, Move to section, Move to a list and an action's form, axMCP's Add server, axTerminal's Add a shell, the item windows' New field, axClaude's New session.

members.when: The focus entered a list from outside it: one opened, Tab or F6 came to it, a notice closed over it, the window started on it (SPEC AX-7.11). Moving inside it is silent.
members.words: NVDA reads the list and its line.
members.apps: Every list of every window, and the answers in the field's place.

members.when: The focus entered a field to type in from outside it: a message field, a document, a name asked for, Find, the command palette, a rename in place (SPEC AX-7.11).
members.words: NVDA reads the field.

members.when: The focus entered a text to read from outside it: a conversation, a help text, a question's words with its buttons, an answer, a file shown read-only (SPEC AX-7.11).
members.words: NVDA reads the text.
members.apps: Every read-only text of every window.
members.note: When the same command just played another sound (a notice that opened by itself, a refusal, a program's question), that sound stands alone and the entry is silent. So for all four kinds.

members.when: The command started work that takes time.
members.words: 'Unlocking x', 'Calling x', 'Searching every list', then after a second 'x, please wait'. Pressed again: 'Working'.
members.apps: axFile, axGIT, axPass, axMCP, axTask, axAutomate, AI help, the updater.
members.note: No sound for a start or an end outside axClaude; the end is the event job-finished.

members.when: The command could not do it.
members.words: One line is spoken with no sound: 'Failed: the reason'. Several lines, or an error with a title, open a notice, and that notice plays the notice sound.
members.note: The error notice chimes even though your own command caused it, because every error notice is marked as coming by itself. A program that an action of an axTask list ran and that failed, or could not be started, plays the same sound with its one line, 'Miss failed, exit code 1', since it ends some time after the key; its output then opens as a plain notice.

members.when: You said no, pressed Escape, or the thing was called off.
members.words: 'Cancelled', 'Delete not run', 'Not started'.

events.title: Something arrived
events.learn: Something came in that you did not ask for at that moment: a line from the program underneath, a file changed by another program, a copy on the clipboard. Mostly there is nothing to do.

members.when: A line of output arrived from the program.
members.words: None with the sound; the line may be spoken after it (reply-spoken).

members.when: Claude called a tool.
members.words: The tool call's row, when Speak tool calls is on.

members.when: Lines of a reply or of a command's output became final and are spoken.
members.words: The lines, joined into one announcement that does not interrupt.

members.when: The program announced something of its own: Claude's bracketed rows such as accept edits on, its detailed view on or off, the conversation cleared.
members.words: The row, or 'Conversation cleared', 'Claude's detailed view is on'.

members.when: The status bar or the title followed the program: working, waiting for your answer, 2 messages waiting, the mode line, the shell's folder.
members.words: None. F8 says the status when you ask.
members.apps: Every window with a status bar.

members.when: Something was copied in any program while axClip keeps the history.
members.words: None; the list is refilled with your place kept.

members.when: Another program changed the file or the folder the window shows. axKit looks when the window comes to the front.
members.words: 'Reloaded, notes.md changed on disk', or 'notes.md changed on disk; Save will ask'. axFile refills silently.
members.apps: axDown, axJSON, axPreview, axFile; the item windows find it at a save.

members.when: Another axKit window handed something to this one: a file to open, files to play, text for the message.
members.words: 'Playing song.mp3', 'Text added to your message from another window, not sent', or NVDA reads the file that opened.
members.apps: axPreview, axMedia, axClaude, the hotkey apps.

events.title: Where the program stands
events.learn: The steps of a turn with the program underneath: it is ready, it began to answer, it is working, it is done, it ended. Rising opens, falling closes.

members.when: The program is ready for your first message or command of this run.
members.words: 'Ready'.

members.when: Claude began its reply.
members.words: 'Responding'.
members.note: axTerminal has no such moment.

members.when: The program is working: Claude on a turn, a command running in the shell.
members.words: None; the status bar says working.

members.when: The program began a turn by itself: work in the background ended and Claude Code took it up, with no message of yours.
members.words: 'Claude goes on by itself'.
members.note: Words only, by a switch of Options, Announcements; the working music has started just before them.

members.when: The turn is over: Claude finished, a shell command finished, a program that an action of an axTask list ran ended without an error, the last file of axMedia's queue ended.
members.words: 'Done'; in axTerminal also 'Failed' or 'Failed, exit code 2'; in axMedia 'End of queue'; in axTask the action's name and 'done'.
members.note: A shell command that failed plays the same sound as one that worked. axMedia's sound has no switch. The call in MainForm.PutAway.cs, for a turn ending while axClaude is put away, is switched off in code.

members.when: The next file of the queue started playing.
members.words: 'Playing song.mp3', when Say each file as it starts is on.

members.when: The program underneath ended or crashed.
members.words: 'Claude stopped', 'The shell ended', 'server stopped (exit code 1)'.
members.note: No sound today, although it ends everything the turn sounds announce.

events.title: Something asks you
events.learn: Something wants an answer or your attention, and you did not start it at that moment. What asks to run code is the loudest of all.

members.when: The program asks a question or a permission.
members.words: The question and the answer you are on, or 'Claude asks', or in axTerminal 'Asks: the row'.
members.note: Two sounds for one thing. Notice (the trill) when axClaude shows the question as a list in the window. Question (two notes) when it cannot be shown as a list, and for axTerminal's guess that a program asks.

members.when: Claude shows a screen that only informs: a side answer, a goal.
members.words: The title and the first line.

members.when: The program took its question back by itself.
members.words: 'Question closed'.

members.when: Claude offers a command for you to run yourself on your computer.
members.words: 'Claude offers a command for you to run', the command, and the caution. Running is never where the list starts.
members.note: Its sound plays wherever the window is, and the taskbar button flashes when the window is behind; the louder background alert never takes its place.

members.when: An AI tool asks to run a command of this window that acts outside the window.
members.words: 'Command offer. Claude asks to run this window's command Delete on a.txt', with the caution; No is the default.
members.apps: Every window but axPass and axClip.
members.note: The same sound as command-offer; docs/axKit/earcons.md proposes a variant of its own.

members.when: A new AI client asks to use axKit.
members.words: 'Claude asks to use axKit', with a consent box; Deny is the default.

members.when: A notice opened that no command of yours asked for: an update was found at start, the settings could not be read or saved or were changed outside axKit, a hotkey is taken, a program is missing, the folder is gone, a repository wants to be trusted, the window met an unexpected error.
members.words: The notice's own text, and Enter is held for a second so that a key already on its way answers nothing.
members.note: The sound can be switched off only in axClaude and axTerminal (with their chimes). In those two windows the settings notes are a line of the conversation and make no sound.

members.when: A notice that comes some time after your command, when its work is finished: 'Claude says', 'x is installed', 'Result of x', 'Report not sent', the unlock question after axPass locked itself.
members.words: The notice's own text.
members.note: No sound, although you may have moved on to something else: these notices are not marked as coming by themselves.

members.when: The program is done or asks while its window is not in front.
members.words: Those of the event behind it; the taskbar button flashes.
members.note: Off at first. When on, it takes the place of the done and question sounds, and plays even with the chimes off.

events.title: Work that goes on behind
events.learn: Work that runs while you do something else, and what is done on your behalf without your hands.

members.when: Claude started work in the background: an agent, a shell, a workflow.
members.words: 'Agent started: the description', when Say background work is on.

members.when: Work is still running in the background.
members.words: None; the status bar counts what runs.

members.when: Work in the background finished.
members.words: 'The description finished', when Say background work is on.

members.when: Work of axKit's own that you started a while ago ended: a copy, a push, an install, a report sent, a server started, a workflow run, a picture's text read.
members.words: The result: 'Pasted 3 items', 'Pushed', 'Git is installed', 'Sent, report 12', 'Text read: 40'. A failure is 'Failed: the reason' or an error notice.
members.apps: axFile, axGIT, axPass, axMCP, axAutomate, axPreview, the updater, the report sender.
members.note: No sound for the end of any work outside axClaude.

members.when: An AI tool ran a command of this window or added a task.
members.words: 'Claude ran Word wrap', joined to what the command itself says; 'Claude added Buy milk to Home'.
members.apps: Every window but axPass and axClip.
members.note: The sound and a flash of the taskbar only when the window is not in front, once for a burst, since NVDA does not speak for a window behind. This is the one use of the notice sound that no switch turns off.

members.when: axPass locked the database: the idle minutes ran out, or Windows was locked.
members.words: 'Locked', then the unlock question.

members.when: axKit did something small for you without a word: a list refilled, the theme repainted, a copied password cleared from the clipboard after 30 seconds, an entry's details read.
members.words: None, on purpose.

events.title: The window itself
events.learn: A window opening, coming back, or changing how its keys work.

members.when: A window opened or came to the front for the first time.
members.words: NVDA reads the title and the focus; what the window had to say before it was in front follows as one sentence.
members.note: No sound today. docs/axKit/earcons.md proposes a short sound of each app's own, and one for the start of axKit.

members.when: A hotkey brought axClaude's window back while the message field still held unsent text.
members.words: 'Unsent message in the field'.
members.note: The recall sound has a second meaning here; its first is a command come back from the history.

members.when: The window had something to tell at its start: a remembered folder on the network was not opened, no project folder is chosen.
members.words: The note, said when the window comes to the front, or a line of the conversation in axClaude and axTerminal.

keys.note: Ctrl+Period opens the Context menu. Ctrl+Slash asks Claude about the window: the answer is a late notice.
Ctrl+Space says the new mode. Space on a row that cannot be checked plays the edge.
In axTask, Ctrl with a digit is also an action key of a list, which is where no-command and refused come from.
F1 and F4 open, F3 lands or says Not found, F5 refreshes, F6 lands in the other pane, F8 says the status.
Ctrl+Enter where the window has no main action plays the edge.
Escape in axClaude's message field only speaks; Shift+Escape interrupts the program.
In axTerminal's command field Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down go through the history: recalled, or the edge at its end.
The three sounds of navigation mode belong to this family: the tick, the buzz and the bonk.
